vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: customer-service-reply
Version: 1.1.1

The skill is a legitimate customer service template generator. The core logic in `scripts/cs.sh` is a Python script that takes user input to generate formatted text responses for various e-commerce scenarios (presale, complaints, refunds, etc.) without any network access, file system manipulation, or sensitive data access.

llm.summary: The skill appears to be a self-contained, local customer-service reply generator (which matches its description) but a pre-scan flagged embedded unicode control characters in the skill text (possible prompt-injection/obfuscation) and the shipped script is large — inspect before running.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included assets: SKILL.md, tips.md, and a script that generates customer service reply templates. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or install steps are requested — the functional footprint is consistent with a local template generator.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are narrow: run scripts/cs.sh with arguments to generate templates. The SKILL.md explicitly states 'purely local generation' and the visible Python code prints canned templates. However the SKILL.md triggered a unicode-control-chars injection warning (see scan findings) which could be used to hide or manipulate content; that is out-of-scope for the stated functionality and should be examined.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; instruction-only plus a bundled script — nothing will be downloaded or installed from the network by the skill itself. This is low-risk compared to fetch-and-run installers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths declared. The skill does not request access to unrelated secrets or cloud services — environment access appears proportionate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not force-enabled (always:false) and does not declare any special persistence or ability to modify other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default but not combined with other elevated privileges.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a local customer-service template generator and largely matches its description, but proceed cautiously because the package contained a scan finding for unicode control characters (which can hide or manipulate text). Before installing or running: 1) Inspect scripts/cs.sh and SKILL.md in a text editor that can show hidden/control characters (or use a hex viewer or `cat -v`/`xxd`). 2) Search the script for network calls (curl, wget, requests, sockets), file reads of sensitive paths, and for any eval/exec of external data. 3) Run the script in an isolated environment (container or VM) as a non-root user. 4) If you plan to use in production, consider running a static analysis or showing the full, untruncated script to someone who can review for hidden behavior. If you find control characters or unexpected network access, do not run the script and remove the skill.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: The SKILL.md content triggered a unicode-control-chars pattern. Control characters are unnecessary for a plain-text instructions file and can be used to obfuscate or inject hidden directives; this is not expected for a local template generator and warrants manual inspection of the raw files (and the large script) before running.
